verses.1: A song of ascents. I raise my eyes toward the mountains. From where will my help come?
verses.2: My help comes from the LORD, the maker of heaven and earth.
verses.3: God will not allow your foot to slip; your guardian does not sleep.
verses.4: Truly, the guardian of Israel never slumbers nor sleeps.
verses.5: The LORD is your guardian; the LORD is your shade at your righthand.
verses.6: By day the sun cannot harm you, nor the moon by night.
verses.7: The LORD will guard you from all evil, will always guard your life.
verses.8: The LORD will guard your coming and going both now and forever.

notes.text: The mountains: possibly Mount Zion, the site of the temple and hence of safety, but more probably mountains as a place of dangers, causing anxiety to the psalmist.
The image of shade, a symbol of protection, is apt: God as shade protects from the harmful effects that ancients believed were caused by the sun and moon.
